The authors used an existing 3D Navier-Stokes code modified to include film cooling considerations.
The C3X vane had 9 rows of film cooling holes, the VKI rotor had 6 rows, and the ACE rotor had 3 rows.
The coolant hole diameters were less than 1 mm for all three blades.
The authors specified experimentally determined temperatures at the blade surface and calculated the wall heat flux.
The Baldwin-Lomax algebraic turbulence model was used, along with Mayle's transition criterion, Forest's model, and Crawford's model.
For the C3X vane, the computational grid had 281 x 45 x 81 grid points.
For the VKI rotor, the heat transfer coefficients were deduced from time-dependent surface temperature measurements using platinum thin-film gages.
For the ACE rotor, thin film platinum resistance thermometers were used to measure the heat transfer.
The incoming flow turbulence intensity was 4.0% for the ACE rotor experiments.
Periodic boundary conditions were used for the C3X vane and VKI rotor analyses, while symmetry conditions were used for the ACE rotor.
The grid size ratio constraint was kept between 0.76 and 1.3 for computational accuracy.
The numerical simulations required about 60 million words of storage and took 20 seconds per iteration on the C-90 supercomputer.
The first case required about 1100 iterations to converge, while subsequent cases required about 300 iterations.
The authors found that the effect of coolant distribution at the hole exit can be as much as 60% on the heat transfer coefficient at the blade suction surface, and 50% at the pressure surface.
The authors compared the numerical results with experimental data for all three blades.
